statement: The construction above produces a smooth connected projective curve C, a reduced divisor Z = q1 + · · · + q6, line bundles H, L, θ, and a basis u = (u1, u2) of H0(C, H) with the following properties. 1. The numerical and canonical data are g(C) = 21, deg H = 4, deg L = 10, L = H + Z, θ = 2L, KC = 4L, where the last isomorphism is normalized by (2.8) and ξ4 |→ γ|C. The curve C has exactly fourth-order contact with the auxiliary elliptic curve Γ at every qj. 2. The pencil u defines a finite degree-four morphism f : C → P1 unramified at every qj, and the values f(qj) are not all equal. The zero divisor of u1 can be chosen to be a reduced fiber disjoint from Z. 8 3. The section dimensions are h0 (C, jH) = j + 1 (0 ≤ j ≤ 3), h0 (C, L) = h0 (C, H + 2Z) = 2, h0 (C, θ) = 3, h0 (C, OC(Z)) = 1, h0 (C, θ + H) = 6. (2.10) More precisely, H0 (C, L) = ξH0 (C, H), H0 (C, H + 2Z) = ξ2 H0 (C, H), H0 (C, θ) = ξ2 H0 (C, 2H). (2.11) In particular r = ξu is a basis of H0(C, L) with simple common zero divisor exactly Z, and every section of θ vanishes twice along Z. 4. For every k ≥ 2, the evaluation map H0 (C, (k + 1)L) −→ H0 (Z, ((k + 1)L)|Z) (2.12) is surjective. 5. The auxiliary data on Γ ⊂ Σ, including the compatible bundle identities, the logarithmic volume Ω, and the quadratic form Q, are as in (2.1) and (2.2); the divisor Z belongs to |M|. The six nonzero vectors wj ∈ H0(Γ, Φ)∗ have the projective evaluation directions at qj, use three distinct directions, and satisfy (2.3), with w2 = 90 = 9 deg L.
